affectedPublicSurfaces: NO seller-facing HTTP surface changes. No `/v1/**` or `/demo/**` route, no response shape, no prompt, no playbook, no ToolSpec. This is a CAPTURE slice: its public surface is the contract collection plus whatever method `PromotionResource` is still missing. Note the code fact the issue phrasing hedges around — `PromotionResource` (`resources/promotion.py`) ALREADY has `create_activity`, `get_activity`, `update_activity`, `update_activity_products` and `deactivate`, and all five paths are ALREADY in `SANDBOX_ALLOWED_REQUESTS`. The realistic diff is therefore captures plus parsing, not new plumbing; if the executor adds a method, the PR must say which call needed it and why the existing one did not serve.

Contract collection rows added, one per observed request/response pair, each carrying request, response, activity id and environment: **B-5a** Create Activity `DIRECT_DISCOUNT` at PRODUCT level; **B-5b** Create Activity `DIRECT_DISCOUNT` at VARIATION level; **A-25a** Get Activity after each create, showing `activity_type: DIRECT_DISCOUNT` and the discount; **B-7a** Update Activity Products attaching a second SKU; **B-8a** Deactivate Activity; **A-25b** Get Activity after deactivation showing `DEACTIVATED`. Row ids follow the collection's existing A-/B- convention (today it runs to A-39 / B-20); if the tip has moved, take the next free ids and say so in the PR.

Two ERROR rows, and they are as load-bearing as the success rows: the collision rejection observed when a second `DIRECT_DISCOUNT` is created for a SKU whose first activity is still ongoing, and the band violation. Both are committed with the vendor's exact `code` and `message`, and the promotion resource maps the collision code to a NAMED error rather than letting it surface as an anonymous `TOOL_ERROR_UNRECOVERABLE` (the scope report's OP-FR-5 gap). Only the codes actually OBSERVED go in — no code is guessed from documentation.

The correction this slice makes to the collection: today B-5 is captured only as `activity_type: "FLASHSALE"` and A-25 shows a `FIXED_PRICE` read. `DIRECT_DISCOUNT` — the single lever both Optimize Product (OP-FR-3) and Clear Excess (CE-FR-2) depend on — appears NOWHERE in code or docs, which makes both workflows v2 by S-NFR-10's own rule until this lands.

State written at the vendor: real `DIRECT_DISCOUNT` activities on SANDBOX_VN shop `7494751643546977923`. Every one of them is deactivated after capture — the epic lock is explicit that no ongoing promotion activity may be left on the sandbox shop, and A-25b is the evidence that it was not.

NOT in scope, and worth naming because the spec is wrong about it: Search/List Activities. `contract-collection.md` A-25 and `endpoints.md` both record that TikTok has NO list/search activity endpoint. Do not add one, do not capture one, do not defer it to v2 as if it were buildable — collision detection is permanently Juli-side.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: `DIRECT_DISCOUNT` stays uncaptured, the promotion resource keeps today's behaviour, and Optimize Product and Clear Excess both stay v2 by S-NFR-10 because their one lever is unobserved. No new exposure, nothing partially applied, no data hazard. The one thing that must still be true is the sandbox hygiene rule: if the walk is abandoned midway, every activity already created is deactivated before stopping.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit. Any new promotion method and any error-code mapping disappear with it; the methods have no production call sites in this slice, so nothing breaks. The committed contract rows are ADDITIVE documentation and an observed shape stays true after a code revert — leaving them is correct. The honest limit of rollback: activities CREATED on the TikTok sandbox seller during the walk are a VENDOR-SIDE effect that a code revert does NOT undo. That is acceptable because the target is the sandbox seller and every activity is deactivated at the end of the walk — but do not claim the revert reverses it. Redeploy of the previous release plus a restart of `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` is sufficient; no downgrade is required.

doNotInfer: NEVER pass a hand-written example response off as a capture. Every committed row is bytes the vendor actually returned, or it is marked 'documented, not captured' in plain words. B-16's example (`contract-collection.md` ~line 1409) is the anti-pattern this epic exists to end.

Do NOT invent a vendor error code. Only the collision and band codes actually OBSERVED go into the rows and into the named-error mapping; a code read from documentation but never seen is recorded as documented-not-captured, never as a mapping.

Do NOT leave an ongoing promotion activity on the sandbox shop. Every activity created during the walk is deactivated, and the proof is a Get Activity showing `DEACTIVATED` for each — an epic-level Architect lock.

Do NOT touch a production write path. Writes go through `SandboxWriteResources` only, and the guard must keep refusing every production write path (ADR-068). Never relax `SandboxOnlyWriteGuard` or `SandboxWriteClientFactory`'s `SANDBOX_AUTH_ID` check to make a call succeed.

Do NOT add a Search/List Activities method or row. TikTok has no such endpoint — `contract-collection.md` A-25 and `endpoints.md` both say so. Collision detection is permanently Juli-side; deferring a non-existent endpoint to v2 is a design error, not a deferral.
Do NOT commit buyer PII, a live token, `sign`, `app_key`, or ciphertext. Use the collection's `{access_token}` / `{sign}` / `{app_key}` / `{shop_cipher}` placeholders.
If a field ADR-090 d.1 or ADR-091 d.2 relies on is ABSENT from the capture, file a documentation-conflict row in PLAN.md §14 with a safe bound. Do not assume it exists and do not code around it.

Do NOT add a ToolSpec, a playbook entry, a prompt, a discount body builder for the agent, or a registry registration. `create_product_discount` is W9-B / W10-A work; this slice ends at the guarded client method and the committed rows.

Do NOT design the 8-rule discount envelope validator here (band, clamp, margin floor, collision, stock bucket, the 300-SKU cap). That is Clear Excess lane work; this slice only OBSERVES what the vendor rejects.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051), `apps/`, `ios/`, `packages/`, `docs/product/design/`, or a sibling issue's context cache — this epic's doNotLoad list.
Bind every test collaborator to the REAL object's signature (`TikTokClient.post`, `.put`, `.get`, `PromotionResource`). A `**kwargs` double proves routing, not that the real call would work.
Do NOT hand-pick a 30-day window or a SKU by editing a fixture to make the capture 'clean'. The window and the SKU are recorded in the row's environment line as they were actually used.
